Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:10:54 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png Trails – beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Buhisan-Puti-Nomolas Community Trail Loop | Buhisan, Labangon, Cebu City | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/buhisan-puti-nomolas-community-trail-loop-buhisan-labangon-cebu-city-2026-gpx/ Sun, 18 Oct 2026 04:00:33 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=2401 The Buhisan-Puti-Nomolas Community Trail Loop is a 4.31 km hiking route in Buhisan, Labangon, Cebu City, that passes through communities and connects to other hiking routes and rest stops. I hiked the loop in October 2026, starting from near Buhisan Elementary School and walking to the trailhead before beginning the main route.

The path was well-trodden, with several intersecting trails, small signs at many junctions, and sections used by local residents, children, and hikers. Along the way, I passed through shaded and exposed areas, encountered muddy and mossy sections, and came across several spots with views of the Cebu City landscape.

Trail Snapshot

0 km0.77 km2.41 km4.73 km
EasyMild
DocumentedOctober 2026
Distance4.31 km (Loop)

This 4.31 km loop begins at approximately 67 m and climbs steadily through the hillside to a peak elevation of about 334 m before descending through thick forest, where vegetation limits views of the surrounding slopes. Near the exit, the trail passes a set of stairs before returning to the starting area.

Duration1.5 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeModerate
0 km0.85 km5.33 km
PavedTrail

4G signal was present across most of the recorded route, with signal detected in 97.6% of observations and confirmed out-of-service conditions accounting for 1.2%. Signal strength ranged from −84 to −124 dBm, with an average of approximately −103 dBm. Reception varied from strong to very weak, indicating inconsistent signal quality along the route. Overall 4G signal quality was poor to fair, with reliable connectivity not guaranteed throughout the trail.

Access

I parked my motorcycle near the suspended bridge, a few meters from Buhisan Elementary School. Parking was free. From there, I walked approximately 800 meters to the starting point because the route’s exit would bring me back near my parked motorcycle. Private vehicles can access the area, and habal-habal services are available, although I had no public transport option listed for this route.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Clear and easy-to-follow trail
✓ Straightforward navigation throughout the route
✓ Frequent communities, farms, or other trail users encountered
✓ No significant cliff exposure or technical terrain
✓ Gentle or gradual elevation changes

On this trail: forest • stairs • sunrise view • valley • viewpoint

Route Description

The trail was generally well-maintained and easy to follow. I passed several intersecting paths, many of which had small trail signs. The route connects with other hiking routes, including those between Starbucks, Buhisan, Pamutan, and Spartan Trail, as well as rest stops such as Bar Cramps and Starbucks.

Goats and chickens were common around the area, while I did not see any cows or carabaos. Dogs were also common near settlements, but the ones I encountered did not display hostile behavior. Hikers, local residents, and children used the paths, and I noticed motorcycle tire tracks in some sections.

Several parts of the route had large trees and dense canopy, while others were fully exposed to direct sunlight. Some sections offered approximately 180-degree views of the Cebu City landscape. Ant activity was noticeable in certain areas.

Trail Conditions

I hiked on a cloudy-to-sunny morning. The trail alternated between dry and muddy sections, with moss making some ascending and descending portions slippery. Shade varied along the route, from dense tree cover to completely exposed sections. Insects were present in a few areas, particularly ants.

The route consisted mostly of trail, with a small portion of road. I did not observe any dangerous cliff exposure during the hike. Although the paths were generally maintained, the mud and moss affected footing in some sections.

Notes

I did not observe extensive farming along the route. The area is part of a protected landscape and contains numerous large trees. The route’s connections to other hiking destinations and rest stops, together with the presence of local residents and other trail users, suggest that it sees regular use. However, I did not verify how frequently hikers use it, particularly on weekends.

]]> Buot Brgy Hall–Sitio Tabla Community Trail | Buot-Taup / Sudlon 1, Cebu City | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/buot-brgy-hall-sitio-tabla-community-trail-buot-taup-sudlon-1-cebu-city-2026-gpx/ Sun, 04 Oct 2026 07:53:13 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1882 The Buot Brgy Hall–Sitio Tabla Community Trail is a 3.34-kilometer point-to-point route from Buot-Taup Barangay Hall toward Sitio Tabla in Cebu City. I hiked it in October 2026, initially planning to complete a loop, but the constant ascent toward Sitio Tabla and the time spent documenting the route slowed my pace enough that I decided to end the hike there.

Most of the route was on trail, with limited shade because of farming on the slopes. The route passes through areas where crops are extensively cultivated and where I encountered livestock, dogs, and mostly local users.

Trail Snapshot

0 km0.34 km3.37 km
EasyTough
DocumentedOctober 2026
Distance3.34 km (Point-to-Point)

This 3.34km route begins at 158 m, climbs steadily through rolling terrain before a steep push to a peak elevation of 736 m around the 3.4 km mark, where the trail concludes.

Duration2 - 2.5 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface98% trail, 2% road

Cellular signal was present across 57% of the recorded route, with LTE availability at 15.8% and dead zones accounting for 43.0%. Coverage was highly intermittent, with extended periods without service and only limited LTE availability, resulting in an overall signal quality assessment of poor.

GPXWikiloc

Access

I parked my motorcycle near the suspended bridge at Buot-Taup Barangay Hall, with no parking fee. Road access to the area is mixed. Public transportation is limited, but habal-habal service is available, as is private vehicle access.

After reaching Sitio Tabla, I hired a habal-habal to take me back to Buot Barangay Hall, where I had left my motorcycle. The fare was ₱150. I have not yet documented the return route between Sitio Tabla and Buot Barangay Hall, so that section will be covered on a future visit.

Why this trail is rated Tough

✓ Long or sustained climbs and descents
✓ Trail may become faint or difficult to identify in places
✓ High route commitment with limited bailout options
✓ Assistance or evacuation may take considerable time

On this trail: farmland • valley

Route Description

I started early with the intention of completing the hike as a loop. My pace was slower than usual because I was documenting the route while dealing with the constant ascent toward Sitio Tabla.

Since this was my second visit, finding the route was considerably easier. Some sections were clear and well-trodden, while other portions passed through cultivated areas. I also came across several new diversion routes.

Much of the route passes through farming areas, with tomatoes, ampalaya, and kamote among the crops being extensively cultivated on the slopes. The route itself was dry during this visit, and the morning shifted between cloudy and sunny conditions.

Trail Conditions

Shade was limited, particularly across the cultivated slopes. There were no stores along the route, and I encountered mostly local users.

Ant activity was particularly noticeable early in the hike. Along the route, I also came across several cows, goats, and carabaos grazing on the slopes and, in some places, directly along the route.

Several territorial dogs were present as well, although most were friendly. I cannot confirm why the dogs behaved this way, though I noted that the route is regularly used by hikers.

The route was approximately 98% trail and 2% road during this hike. In terms of water, I carried the equivalent of at least 2 liters.

Notes

The route does not involve dangerous cliff exposure. However, the combination of sustained climbing, limited shade, and cultivated sections made the ascent toward Sitio Tabla slower for me on this visit.

I ultimately changed the planned loop into a point-to-point hike and ended at Sitio Tabla, returning to Buot Barangay Hall by habal-habal rather than completing a loop hike.

]]> Buot-Samboryo-Babag Ridge-Guila Trail | Buot-Taup, Cebu City | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/buot-samboryo-babag-ridge-guila-trail-buot-taup-cebu-city-2026-gpx/ Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:08:15 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1297 The Buot–Samboryo–Babag Ridge–Guila Trail is a roughly 7.58 km point-to-point hike in the Buot-Taup area of Cebu City, with paved-road access at both ends. I followed a shorter reverse variation of my earlier Buot–Guila-Guila–Cabatbatan–Samboryo Trail Loop, including about 2.72 km of previously unvisited trail that I refer to here as the Phase 1 Babag Ridge Trail.

Much of the ridge was open and covered in cogon grass, while several sections closer to the communities passed under better tree cover. I did this hike in September 2026.

Trail Snapshot

MILD
DocumentedSeptember 2026
Distance7.58 km (Point-to-Point)

The 7.58 km route features a total elevation gain of 533 m, characterized by multiple major climbs that reach a peak elevation of 660 m at km 2.88. The remainder of the course consists primarily of significant descents alongside an additional climb, totaling 506 m of elevation loss.

Duration2-3 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeModerate
0 km0.77 km6.94 km7.54 km
PavedUnpavedTrail

Cellular signal was present across 86.8% of the route, with LTE availability recorded at 84.2% and dead zones accounting for 13.2%. Coverage was intermittent with multiple drops into dead zones, resulting in an overall signal quality assessment of moderate.

GPXWikiloc

Access

I left my motorcycle near the suspended bridge close to the Barangay Buot barangay hall, where I did not pay a parking fee. From there, I crossed the bridge and started the ascent toward Samboryo. Public transport in the area is limited, although habal-habal and private vehicle access are available.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Mostly clear trail with occasional navigation awareness required
✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some isolated sections between communities
✓ Limited turnaround or exit options

On this trail: ridge

Route Description

From the bridge, I climbed toward Samboryo for approximately 2.41 km. Early in the hike, the trail widened enough to resemble an unpaved road, but that section ended abruptly and narrowed again into a rocky ascending path.

The climb continued to a junction where one trail descended toward Cabatbatan and the other continued onto the Babag Ridge Trail. This ridge section covered approximately 2.72 km, beginning around km 2.16 and ending near km 4.88 of the hike.

I passed small clusters of communities during the earlier part of the route but did not see extensive farming there. A few goats and cows were beside or near the trail. I also noticed relatively few dogs until I reached Barangay Guila-Guila near the end of the hike, where I began seeing larger groups.

Some of the first sections of the Babag Ridge Trail had good tree cover extending for several meters. Most of the ridge, however, remained relatively open, with little tree cover and cogon grass across much of the surrounding ground.

The path itself was generally well-trodden and easy to follow. Despite the mountain setting, I saw little vegetation growing across the trail, and the route appeared to receive regular use from local residents and livestock.

Trail Conditions

The trail was dry during this hike, with cloudy to sunny conditions in the morning. I spent roughly 81% of the route on trail and 19% on road. Insect activity was low, and most of the people I saw were local residents.

Stores were available near the communities along the route. I also saw small spring catchments, particularly around Guila-Guila, where hoses had been connected to spring sources so water could flow downhill toward homes by gravity.

Notes

Pig raising was especially noticeable along this route. Compared with other hiking routes I have visited, I passed more households or areas where pigs were being raised.

]]> Buot-Guila-Cabatbatan-Samboryo Trail Loop | Buot-Taup, Cebu City | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/buot-guila-cabatbatan-samboryo-trail-loop-buot-taup-cebu-city-2026-gpx/ Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:32:12 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1267 The Buot-Guila-Cabatbatan-Samboryo Trail Loop is a 12.75-kilometer loop through Buot-Taup, Guila-Guila, Babag Ridge, Dam-an, Cabatbatan, and Samboryo in Cebu City. I started near the suspended community bridge by the Barangay Buot-Taup Hall and initially followed the road toward Guila-Guila before climbing toward Babag Ridge and continuing through the mountain sections.

About 45% of the route was trail and 55% unpaved or concrete road, with moderate shade and many stores near the communities. I did this hike in August 2026 on a cloudy-sunny morning, and the trail was dry, with very few insects and almost no human traffic once I reached the high mountain sections.

Trail Snapshot

0 km3.55 km4.91 km9.49 km12.75 km
EasyMildTough
DocumentedAugust 2026
Distance12.75 km (Loop)

The 12.75 km route has a total elevation gain of 625 m and features terrain with multiple major climbs. The elevation profile includes five significant ascents reaching major peaks of 551 m at km 4.97 and 408 m at km 7.7, followed by a final descent of 395 m from km 10.3 to 12.69.

Duration4-5 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeModerate

Cellular signal was present across 46.7% of the route with an identical 46.7% LTE availability, while dead zones accounted for 53.3% of the recorded points. Coverage remained intermittent with multiple drops into dead zones, resulting in an overall signal quality assessment of moderate.

GPXWikiloc

Access

I parked my motorcycle near the suspended bridge by the Barangay Buot-Taup Hall. There was no parking fee, and the road to the area was concrete. Public transportation was limited, while habal-habal and private vehicle access were available.

Because the loop exits back at the bridge, I first had to hike about 3.4 kilometers toward Guila-Guila. From there, I passed through a small hillside community and relied on directions from friendly locals to find the way.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Mostly clear trail with occasional navigation awareness required
✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some isolated sections between communities
✓ Limited turnaround or exit options

On this trail: bridge • cliff • farmland • forest • ridge • roads

Route Description

The ascent began immediately after the Guila-Guila hillside community and continued steadily toward Babag Ridge. Some sections were already being reclaimed by thick vegetation despite the recent Pamutan Trailfest 2026, and I noted that these portions could become difficult to follow within a few months.

Near the approach to Babag Ridge, farming activity kept the pathways clearer and more maintained. I then continued descending through the mountain sections toward Dam-an and Cabatbatan before ascending again toward Samboryo.

Along the way, I passed hillside farms and roadside plantings of cassava, corn, eggplant, and banana. Several concrete spring catchments had also been built across the agricultural areas for irrigation.

Two large cows blocked the pathway at one point, so I had to negotiate my way around them. I also passed two sections with heavy tree canopies that gave solid shade: one after Babag Ridge toward Dam-an and another near Samboryo on the way back toward Buot-Taup.

Trail Conditions

The trail was dry during my hike. Shade coverage was moderate overall, with the two heavily canopied sections providing more substantial cover. I encountered only a few insects throughout the route.

Stores were common near the communities, while the higher mountain sections had very few structures. Most houses were concentrated along the main roads on the lower hillsides.

Notes

I encountered dense groups of dogs near residential areas, but the open mountain sections were completely clear of animals. Human traffic was also limited: I met locals during the initial ascent in Guila-Guila and around the road crossings toward Dam-an, Cabatbatan, and Samboryo, but saw no other people on the high mountain trail.

Several stretches had moderate to high cliff exposure, although thick foliage largely hid the drop-offs. The route also had two large cows occupying the trail during my passage.

The descent toward Samboryo also showed how the route changes when approached from the opposite direction. From Buot-Taup toward Samboryo, the same section would involve a sustained climb on a narrow, rocky track.

]]> Inayagan-Cantao-an-Pangilatan Peak Community Trail Loop | Cantao-an, Naga City | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/inayagan-cantao-an-pangilatan-peak-community-trail-loop-cantao-an-naga-city-2026-gpx/ Fri, 21 Aug 2026 05:37:09 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1235 The Pangilatan Peak Loop is a 5.26 km loop hike located across Inayagan and Cantao-an in Naga City. I followed a route that began high on the mountain, descended toward the Metro Cebu Expressway, and circled back up past several rural communities to reach the peak.

The hike was characterized by a long, steep initial descent over fine scree and sharp rock, followed by road walking through active construction areas and local settlements. A morning haze hung across the valley during this sunny hike, which I completed in August 2026.

Trail Snapshot

0 km1.52 km3.48 km5.31 km
EasyMild
DocumentedAugust 2026
Distance5.26 km (Loop)

This 5.26 km loop hike features an overall elevation gain of approximately 317 m, ranging between 38 m and 313 m in altitude, with smoothed maximum grades reaching roughly +28% uphill and -26% downhill, and its toughest climb occurring on the sustained ascent to Pangilatan Peak between kilometer 3.6 and 4.2.

Duration2.5 - 3 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface60% trail, 40% road

Cellular signal was present across 97.5% of the recorded points with 2.5% dead zones, while LTE connectivity was available along 92.5% of the route alongside 5% GSM coverage. The overall signal quality was assessed as good, with no weak signal or intermittent coverage observed.

GPXWikiloc

Access

I started at the foot of Pangilatan Peak, where motorcycle parking was available without a fee. The jump-off point was accessible by concrete road and could be reached by private vehicle. Public transportation to the area was limited, though habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some isolated sections between communities
✓ Moderate route commitment
✓ Limited turnaround or exit option

On this trail: cliff • forest • peak • roads • valley

Route Description

Since the jump-off point sits on top of the mountain, I began with a continuous 1.22 km descent toward the lowlands. The footpath was covered with loose scree and razor-sharp rock surfaces, requiring careful footing on the way down.

At the bottom of the hill, the trail intersected the active Metro Cebu Expressway project, where I walked through dirt, dust, and mud near large construction machinery. After passing the construction corridor, the route turned uphill along the road, leading through several residential communities before returning to Pangilatan Peak to complete the loop.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout the morning, and trail surfaces stayed completely dry. Tree cover was limited, leaving most of the route exposed to the sun. Small local stores were open near the communities along the back half of the loop, though carrying at least 2 liters of water was necessary.

I ran into high insect activity along the footpaths, and the crowd consisted mostly of locals, along with a few joggers and hikers near Pangilatan Peak. Approximately 60% of the route followed dirt and rock trails, while the remaining 40% consisted of roads.

Additional Notes

Dogs were present in large numbers along the trails and near the settlements, making a trekking pole especially helpful both for stability on the loose rock and for keeping animals at a distance. Although the sweeping valley landscape remained broad and open, morning haze kept the view from looking as crisp as on my previous visit.

Early morning hikers and joggers mostly used the concrete road leading to the peak, while others continued onto the mountain path to finish their hike.

]]> Pangilatan Peak Loop | Cantao-an, Naga City | 2024 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/pangilatan-peak-loop-cantao-an-naga-city-2024-gpx/ Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:10:10 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1066 The Pangilatan Peak Loop is a documented 2.56 km loop hike in Cantao-an, Naga City. I followed a combination of community trails and concrete roads leading to Pangilatan Peak before returning to the starting point. The route was short, easy to follow, and passed through areas with regular local activity, making it one of the more accessible mountain hikes in the area.

I completed this hike in April 2024 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedApril 2024
Distance2.56 km (Loop)
Duration1 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter

Access

I started at the foot of Pangilatan Peak, where motorcycle parking was available without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

On this trail: peak • sunrise view • sunset view • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by following established community trails that gradually climbed toward Pangilatan Peak. Navigation remained straightforward throughout the hike, with the summit only a short walk from the jump-off. After reaching the peak, I continued around the loop using a combination of trails and concrete roads before returning to the starting point.

The route connected with several other hiking trails around Cantao-an, making Pangilatan Peak a natural junction for longer hikes in the area. During my visit, I encountered local residents along the route and a few hikers near the summit.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Much of the route had limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Stores were available near the surrounding communities, and mobile signal remained strong from start to finish. Approximately 60% of the loop followed trails, while the remaining 40% used concrete roads. I noticed only a few insects during the hike.

Additional Notes

The jump-off was only a short distance from the summit, making Pangilatan Peak one of the easiest mountain viewpoints to reach in Naga City. The peak also has a campsite where hikers occasionally stay overnight. During favorable weather, a sea of clouds can sometimes form below, covering Barangay Guindaruhan.

]]> Incomplete/ Buhisan Mini Forest Loop https://beesayatv.com/trails/incomplete-buhisan-mini-forest-loop/ Mon, 20 Jul 2026 12:19:15 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=929 This route is still being explored. The Trail Atlas currently shows only the section that I was able to verify during my most recent field visit.

The exploration took place in June 2026 with the goal of verifying a downloaded GPX route that appeared to form a loop through the Buhisan forest near the Buhisan Reservoir. I was able to follow the trail deep into the forest before deciding to turn back.

The first part of the route was well-trodden and appeared to be used regularly by both hikers and local residents. During the hike, one local resident mentioned that the loop eventually passed through a densely vegetated section, which I later reached. The trail crossed a small river where the continuation remained visible on the opposite bank. Farther ahead, however, erosion made it difficult to locate the trail, and I could no longer confidently identify where it continued. I ended the exploration at that point and retraced my steps.

Based on what I saw, the route may be easier to verify by approaching it from the opposite direction during a future field visit.

The forested section contained several spring water collection points with multiple water pipes, suggesting that local residents still access the area. I also encountered several thorny plants, and in many places the trail had become faint and difficult to distinguish. Some sections showed heavy erosion that may have resulted from strong water flow.

A future visit will require additional time. The dense vegetation and heavy tree cover make the footpaths difficult to follow, while also limiting how much can be confirmed using satellite imagery alone.

Naupa-Balirong Trail Loop | Cogon / Balirong, Naga | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/cogon-mt-naupa-balirong-trail-loop-cogon-balirong-naga-2026-gpx/ Sat, 18 Jul 2026 23:17:16 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=862 The Cogon–Mt. Naupa area before descending toward Balirong and returning to Cogon.

The hike featured rolling terrain with frequent short climbs and descents instead of one sustained ascent, creating a steady workout. Although much of the route passed near communities, a few quieter sections required extra attention where the trail became faint. I completed this hike in July 2026.

Trail Snapshot

MILD
DocumentedJuly 2026
Distance11 km (Loop)

This 11.25 km loop hike features an overall elevation gain of approximately 489 m, spanning altitudes from 63 m to 508 m, with smoothed maximum grades reaching roughly +28% uphill and -30% downhill, and its toughest climb occurring on the steep approach to the Mt. Naupa peak between kilometer 3.0 and 3.6.

Duration3.5 - 4 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface30% trail, 70% road

Access

I started near Cogon Chapel, where motorcycle parking was available without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Mostly clear trail with occasional navigation awareness required
✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some isolated sections between communities
✓ Assistance may require additional time to reach

On this trail: farmland • rolling hills • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by following community roads and trails toward Mt. Naupa, where the route alternated between open countryside and well-used footpaths. Most of the trail was easy to follow, and I regularly crossed paths with local residents and livestock while moving through the area. Near the Mt. Naupa summit, I also encountered a few other hikers.

After leaving the Mt. Naupa area, I reached sections where cultivated farmland had replaced parts of the original trail, making it take a little longer to locate the next segment. The descent toward Balirong also included a faint section of trail that appeared to receive less foot traffic. Near the Balirong exit, I crossed a small stream before continuing toward Cogon. The final part of the hike followed Cogon Road, where a steady uphill climb led back to Cogon Chapel and completed the loop.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained cloudy throughout my hike. Much of the route was exposed with limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Stores were available whenever I passed through communities, and mobile signal remained strong for most of the hike with only a few dead spots.

I mostly encountered local residents, along with a few hikers near Mt. Naupa, and insect activity was noticeably high. Approximately 30% of the route followed trails, while the remaining 70% used roads.

Additional Notes

The rolling terrain provided a steady rhythm of climbs and descents without any prolonged ascent or descent. During my visit, several narrow road improvement projects appeared unfinished, although I did not see any active construction work.

It was also mango season, and many plantations had fallen fruit scattered beneath the trees. Some roadside sections passed pig-raising areas where livestock odors were noticeable. I also saw cows along the route, although none blocked the trail. Throughout the hike, I had several friendly conversations with local residents, who were welcoming and helpful.

]]> Guindaruhan-Estaka Trail Loop | Guindaruhan, Minglanilla | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/guindaruhan-estaka-trail-loop-guindaruhan-minglanilla-2026-gpx/ Wed, 15 Jul 2026 13:56:17 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=793 The Guindaruhan–Estaka Trail Loop is a documented 3.04 km loop hike in Barangay Guindaruhan, Minglanilla. I followed a combination of quiet community roads and established footpaths that descended into the valley of Cutod Falls before returning through Estaka to complete the loop.

The route remained easy to follow throughout, despite sections where vegetation partially covered the trail. I completed this hike in March 2026 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedMarch 2026
Distance3.12 km (Loop)

This 3.12 km loop hike features a total elevation gain of approximately 100 m, spanning altitudes from 30 m to 145 m, with smoothed maximum grades reaching roughly +22% uphill and -25% downhill, and its toughest climb occurring on the sustained ascent out of the valley between kilometer 0.6 and 1.3.

Duration1.5 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface40% trail, 60% road
GPXWikiloc

Access

I started near Guindaruhan National High School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The trailhead was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Clear and easy-to-follow trail
✓ Frequent communities, farms, or other trail users encountered
✓ No significant cliff exposure or technical terrain
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ Gentle or gradual elevation changes

On this trail: river crossing • waterfall

Route Description

I began by walking along a gradually ascending concrete road through Barangay Guindaruhan before passing the small communities of Purok Cacao. From there, the route left the road and followed a narrow footpath descending toward Cutod Falls. Although dense vegetation covered parts of the trail during my visit, I had no difficulty following the route.

After reaching the waterfalls, I continued through the valley on well-established footpaths that local residents regularly used as a shortcut to Guindaruhan proper. The loop then climbed out through Estaka, where I followed a concrete road past more communities before returning to the starting point.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Much of the route had limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Mobile signal was strong near the start before becoming intermittent farther along the route. I found stores near the communities, encountered mostly local residents, and noticed many insects. Approximately 40% of the route followed trails, while the remaining 60% used concrete roads.

Additional Notes

The trail around Cutod Falls remained well-defined despite the overgrown vegetation in some sections. I also noticed litter around the waterfalls, even though signs reminding visitors not to leave trash were present.

]]> Incomplete/ Campagao Peak Area https://beesayatv.com/trails/incomplete-campagao-peak-area/ Mon, 13 Jul 2026 13:26:26 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=775 This route is still being explored. The Trail Atlas currently shows only the section that I was able to verify during my most recent field visit.

The exploration took place in July 2026 with the goal of verifying a downloaded GPX route that appeared to form a loop around Campagao Peak. I followed the route to a pocket forest with a small residential settlement before deciding to turn back.

After reaching the settlement, I asked several local residents about the continuation of the trail, but the directions I received were inconsistent. One steep trail appeared to continue uphill, although I could not confirm where it led or whether it connected to the intended loop. Rather than continue without verification, I returned by retracing the established Campagao Peak trail.

Based on what I saw, the route may be easier to verify by approaching it from the opposite direction during a future field visit.

The junction where this route branches from the Campagao Peak trail was faint and easy to miss, suggesting that relatively few people use it. A short distance beyond the junction, however, the trail became well-defined. I also noted that another trail may provide direct access to the pocket forest without passing through the Campagao Peak route.

A future visit will require additional time. Dense vegetation and tree cover obscure the footpaths, making it difficult to verify the route using satellite imagery alone.
